title: Console API: expose rollout auto-actions (auto-pause/auto-rollback/suppress) with filtering + RBAC
creator: Chloe Martin
content:
Goal
Expose auto-actions triggered by the rollout controller (auto-pause, auto-rollback, suppression/override decisions) in the Console backend API so the UI can render an audit timeline and operators can query events for incident triage.

This ticket covers:
- Read APIs (list + detail) for rollout auto-actions
- Filtering/pagination requirements
- RBAC constraints (who can view which fields / which scopes)
- Auditability alignment with ADR-0128

Non-goals
- Implementing the controller decisions themselves (see ENG-4821 / rollout controller PRs)
- Implementing admin override mutation endpoints (tracked separately; ensure RBAC model won’t block future write APIs)

Background / context
Rollout controller will emit structured audit events for auto-decisions (rollback/pause/suppress) and we need Console API endpoints to:
- show “what happened and why” in the rollout UI
- link to relevant SLO monitors and dashboards
- support support/SRE workflows (filter by time window / action type)

References
- Confluence ADR: adr-0128-rollout-audit-trail-schema-for-auto-actions
- Design spec: rollout-controller-slo-monitoring-integration-design
- Observability naming: rollouts-slo-metrics-naming-and-labeling
- Related PRs (in flight):
  - PR: redwood/pr-28427-console-api-expose-rollout-auto-actions
  - PR: redwood/pr-28435-add-rollout-audit-events-to-event-stream

Proposed API (Console backend)
1) List auto-actions for a rollout
GET /console/v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/auto-actions
Query params:
- since: RFC3339 timestamp (optional)
- until: RFC3339 timestamp (optional)
- action: comma-separated enum filter (optional) values: PAUSE, ROLLBACK, SUPPRESS, NOOP
- outcome: comma-separated enum filter (optional) values: TRIGGERED, SUPPRESSED, SKIPPED, ERROR
- limit: int (default 50, max 200)
- cursor: opaque pagination token (optional)

Response (shape; exact naming tbd but keep stable once shipped):
- items: array
- next_cursor: string|null

AutoAction item fields (minimum for MVP UI + triage):
- id: stable id (prefer audit event id)
- rollout_id
- rollout_step_id (optional)
- action: enum (PAUSE|ROLLBACK|SUPPRESS|NOOP)
- outcome: enum (TRIGGERED|SUPPRESSED|SKIPPED|ERROR)
- decided_at: RFC3339
- reason_code: enum string (e.g., SLO_BREACH, MONITOR_STALE, MIN_SAMPLE_NOT_MET, DEBOUNCE_ACTIVE, INCIDENT_OVERRIDE)
- reason_summary: short human-readable summary (safe to display)
- policy_version: string (config version/hash)
- policy_name: optional template name
- monitor_ids: list of strings (can be empty when suppressed due to missing monitor)
- metrics_snapshot_ref: string (pointer/handle; do not inline high-cardinality payload)
- evaluation_window: string (e.g., "fast=5m slow=30m")
- scope: string (flattened for now; see notes below)
- actor: string (e.g., "rollout-controller" or "admin:<user_id>")
- correlation_id: string (trace/correlation)
- links: list of strings (Grafana dashboard URL, monitor definition URL, internal logs)

NOTE on scope flattening:
The audit schema includes route/model_version/region/customer_tier; for Console API we can either:
(a) expose a single normalized string like: "route=/v1/chat model=llama-3.1-70b@2026-02-20 region=us-east-1 tier=dedicated"
(b) expose separate fields.
Given the JSON-no-nesting constraint doesn’t apply to API responses, we can still do (b) in real code; for MVP, keep UI simple and include both a human-readable scope string + stable keys in the backend model.

2) Global search endpoint (optional for MVP; required for SRE workflows)
GET /console/v1/auto-actions
Query params:
- service_id or route_id (optional)
- region (optional)
- customer_tier (optional)
- action/outcome (optional)
- since/until (optional)
- limit/cursor

If time-constrained, we can postpone global search and rely on rollout-scoped list + existing event stream tooling.

Data source
Preferred: read from the audit events table/index that’s fed by the event stream emitter (PR-28435). Console API should not query the controller directly.

Implementation notes
- Storage: ensure events are queryable by rollout_id + decided_at with an index; typical query pattern is “latest N events”.
- Pagination: cursor should encode decided_at + id to make ordering stable (desc by decided_at, tie-break by id).
- Consistency: it’s OK if events are eventually consistent within ~30–60s; UI should show “may be delayed”.
- Field hygiene:
  - Do NOT inline raw metrics time series. Only return snapshot handle + a couple of precomputed summary strings (reason_summary, evaluation_window).
  - Avoid monitor definition payloads; return monitor_ids + links.

RBAC / security requirements
We need clear, enforceable rules for who can see what:
- Base requirement: any user who can view a rollout can view the existence of auto-actions for that rollout.
- Tenant boundary: events must be scoped to the same workspace/org as the rollout; no cross-tenant leakage.
- Dedicated/Private additional constraints:
  - Some customers restrict visibility by environment/region. Follow existing rollout RBAC checks.
- Sensitive fields:
  - metrics_snapshot_ref may reveal internal identifiers; OK for internal users and org members, but do not expose anything that can be used to traverse other tenants.
  - links should be filtered: external-facing Console should only show customer-safe links; internal-only Grafana links should be behind an internal permission (e.g., "observability:read:internal").

Proposed RBAC gates (match existing patterns):
- rollout:auto_actions:read -> required for list/detail
- rollout:read -> implied/required (existing)
- observability:internal_links:read -> controls whether internal Grafana/log links are included

Decision needed (open)
Do we implement link filtering in the API response serializer (recommended), or do we return all links and let the UI hide? API-side filtering is safer.

Acceptance criteria
- API endpoint returns auto-actions for a rollout, ordered newest-first, paginated.
- Filtering by action/outcome + time window works and is covered by unit tests.
- RBAC enforced:
  - unauthorized users get 403
  - internal-only links omitted when user lacks permission
- Schema is aligned with ADR-0128 (required fields present, naming consistent enough to map 1:1).
- Basic performance: P95 < 200ms for last-50 query at typical load.
- Audit trail rendered in Console UI can consume the API without additional joins beyond fetching the rollout.

Test plan
- Unit tests: RBAC, pagination stability, filtering.
- Integration test (staging): emit a synthetic auto-pause event via event stream, verify it appears via API within expected delay.
- Negative tests: attempt to query rollout_id from another org; ensure 404/403 depending on current conventions.

Rollout plan
- Behind feature flag: console.auto_actions_api
- Enable in staging first (used by DES/ENG-4833 UI work).
- In prod: enable for internal users first (Redwood org), then expand.

Updates

- Drafted endpoint shape + pagination strategy; synced with Jada on event IDs and correlation_id.
- Open question: whether the audit emitter will include policy_name vs only policy_version.

2026-02-18 (Felix)
- Implemented list endpoint in branch; currently returns action/outcome/decided_at/reason_summary/monitor_ids/policy_version.
- Blocked on final event stream schema from PR-28435 (need stable field names for reason_code + metrics_snapshot_ref).

2026-02-21 (Chloe)
- Please ensure the endpoint supports filtering by action + outcome (SRE asked for quickly finding SUPPRESS due to MONITOR_STALE).
- Add explicit internal-link gating; do not assume Console is internal-only.

2026-02-25 (Felix)
- Added RBAC gates: rollout:auto_actions:read and observability:internal_links:read.
- Added serializer filtering for links; internal Grafana URLs only when internal_links permission is present.
- Next: wire metrics_snapshot_ref once available; add integration test using staging event stream.
